A preset is a collection of options that: A preset is a collection of options that will provide a certain encoding speed to compression ratio.
A starting point for every workflow. Mak: A starting point for every workflow. Make it yours.
Adjusts x264 and x265 for a type of cont: Adjusts x264 and x265 for a type of content. The list shows the tunes the chosen encoder accepts; other encoders have none.
Analyze a source, then use Auto to choos: Analyze a source, then use Auto to choose compatible settings without upscaling.
Analyze your source to get tailored sett: Analyze your source to get tailored settings.
Apply a wavelet based denoiser. It trans: Apply a wavelet based denoiser. It transforms each frame from the video input into the wavelet domain, using Cohen-Daubechies-Feauveau 9/7. Then it applies some filtering to the obtained coefficients. It does an inverse wavelet transform after. Due to wavelet properties, it should give a nice smoothed result, and reduced noise, without blurring picture features.
Attempt to fix small changes in horizont: Attempt to fix small changes in horizontal and/or vertical shift. This filter helps remove camera shake from hand-holding a camera, bumping a tripod, moving on a vehicle, etc.
Audio bit rate. For stereo AAC, 128k sou: Audio bit rate. For stereo AAC, 128k sounds good and 192k or more is hard to tell from the original. Opus sounds good from about 96k.
Audio dynamic range compression: brings: Audio dynamic range compression: brings quiet and loud parts closer together, which sounds louder and punchier. Higher values are stronger; 33 leaves it off.
Brightens or darkens the midtones while: Brightens or darkens the midtones while leaving black and white alone. 10 is neutral; below darkens and above brightens. 0 leaves it unchanged.
Browser preview — run the desktop app to: Browser preview — run the desktop app to access files, install FFmpeg and encode.
Build, fine-tune and run your next encod: Build, fine-tune and run your next encode.
Caps resolution, frame rate and bit rate: Caps resolution, frame rate and bit rate so a specific device can decode the file. For example, 3.1 fits 720p and 4.0/4.1 fit 1080p30. Leave it on None unless something requires it.
Choose a release below or import ffmpeg: Choose a release below or import ffmpeg and ffprobe from your computer.
Choose your language and extend the tran: Choose your language and extend the translation catalog.
Colour intensity. 0 leaves it unchanged,: Colour intensity. 0 leaves it unchanged, -100 is black and white, 100 doubles it and 200 triples it.

Constant Rate Factor (CRF). Use this rat: Constant Rate Factor (CRF). Use this rate control if you want to keep the best quality and care less about the file size.
Create the filtergraph specified by <em>: Create the filtergraph specified by filtergraph and use it to filter the stream. This is an alias for -filter:a, see the -filter option.
Create the filtergraph specified by filtergraph and use it to filter the stream. This is an alias for -filter:v, see the -filter option.
Cut out part of the input instead of con: Cut out part of the input instead of converting all of it. Enabling this shows the start and stop times.
Deinterlace the input video (\"yadif\" m: Deinterlace the input video ("yadif" means "yet another deinterlacing filter").
Delay the audio by the given number of m: Delay the audio by the given number of milliseconds, to fix audio/video sync.
Delays the audio by this many millisecon: Delays the audio by this many milliseconds, to fix audio that plays ahead of the picture. Needs an audio codec other than Copy.
Difference between light and dark areas. 0 leaves it unchanged; negative flattens the picture, positive makes it punchier.
Do not overwrite output files, and exit: Do not overwrite output files, and exit immediately if a specified output file already exists.
Drop media and subtitle files here: Drop media and subtitle files here
Dump full command line and log output to: Dump full command line and log output to a file named program-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS.log in the current directory.
Edit JSON argument arrays. Each array ru: Edit JSON argument arrays. Each array runs as one FFmpeg process; no shell is used.
Evens out brightness that pulses from fr: Evens out brightness that pulses from frame to frame, as in timelapses or footage under flickering lights.
Every encode, from the first frame to th: Every encode, from the first frame to the final file.
How colour is stored in each frame. Leav: How colour is stored in each frame. Leave it on auto unless something requires a specific format.
How far the bit rate may swing around th: How far the bit rate may swing around the target before max rate is enforced. Often 1–2× the max rate; smaller means a steadier bit rate.
How much ffmpeg prints while it runs. Er: How much ffmpeg prints while it runs. Error shows only problems; Info is ffmpeg's default; Debug and Trace are for troubleshooting.
How the encoder decides how many bits to: How the encoder decides how many bits to spend.
Install once. Choose the right engine fo: Install once. Choose the right engine for each project.
Language packs only contain interface te: Language packs only contain interface text. Commands, paths and media metadata are never translated.
Les fichiers existants sont protégés par: Les fichiers existants sont protégés par défaut.
Makes the whole picture lighter or darke: Makes the whole picture lighter or darker. 0 leaves it unchanged.
Maximum frames between keyframes. Smalle: Maximum frames between keyframes. Smaller values make seeking and stream segments snappier at the cost of size. A keyframe every 2 seconds (e.g. 48 at 24 fps) is common for streaming.
Missing translations fall back to Englis: Missing translations fall back to English. Language availability is not a verified population coverage figure.
Move the index (moov atom) to the beginn: Move the index (moov atom) to the beginning of the file. This operation can take a while, and will not work in various situations such as fragmented output, thus it is not enabled by default.
Moves the MP4 index to the front of the: Moves the MP4 index to the front of the file so playback can start before the whole file downloads. Turn it on for video served on the web.
Number of audio channels. Converting to: Number of audio channels. Converting to fewer channels mixes them down; ffmpeg is told to avoid clipping while doing so.
Output frames per second. Lowering it dr: Output frames per second. Lowering it drops frames and raising it duplicates them; it does not create slow motion (use Speed for that).
Output height in pixels. Use -1 to keep: Output height in pixels. Use -1 to keep the aspect ratio from the width, or -2 to do the same while rounding to an even number.
Output width in pixels. Use -1 to keep t: Output width in pixels. Use -1 to keep the aspect ratio from the height, or -2 to do the same while rounding to an even number, which most encoders need.
Plays the video faster or slower by resc: Plays the video faster or slower by rescaling its timestamps. Only the video changes speed, so the audio will drift out of sync; consider removing the audio.
Quality level for constant-quality encod: Quality level for constant-quality encoding. Lower is better quality and a bigger file. For x264, 23 is the default and about 18 looks visually lossless; x265 defaults to 28. Each step of about 6 roughly halves or doubles the file size.
Raw encoder settings passed straight to: Raw encoder settings passed straight to x264 or x265 as key=value pairs separated by colons, e.g. keyint=72:scenecut=0. Only used with those two codecs.
Reduces noise and grain. Stronger settin: Reduces noise and grain. Stronger settings remove more noise but also soften fine detail.
Reduces small camera shake from hand-hel: Reduces small camera shake from hand-held shots or a bumped tripod. The edges uncovered as the frame shifts are filled in from the picture.
Remove banding artifacts from input vide: Remove banding artifacts from input video. It works by replacing banded pixels with average value of referenced pixels.
Remove judder produced by partially inte: Remove judder produced by partially interlaced telecined content.
Removes the comb-like lines of interlace: Removes the comb-like lines of interlaced video from old TV, DVDs or 1080i cameras. Leave it off for normal progressive video.
Removes the uneven motion left in partia: Removes the uneven motion left in partially telecined footage, where film was converted to TV frame rates.
Resizes the video. The presets set one s: Resizes the video. The presets set one side and keep the source aspect ratio for the other; Custom lets you enter both.
Restricts the encoder to a feature set s: Restricts the encoder to a feature set so older or limited devices can play the file. Leave it on None unless a device or service asks for one.
Samples per second. 48k is standard for: Samples per second. 48k is standard for video and 44.1k for music. Raising it above the source adds size but no quality.
Save the current settings without source: Save the current settings without source or destination paths.
Scale (resize) the input video, using th: Scale (resize) the input video, using the libswscale library.
Scales the loudness: 100 leaves it uncha: Scales the loudness: 100 leaves it unchanged, 50 halves it, 200 doubles it. Large increases can clip. Needs an audio codec other than Copy.
Select the pass number (1 or 2). It is u: Select the pass number (1 or 2). It is used to do two-pass video encoding.
Send program-friendly progress informati: Send program-friendly progress information to stdout.
Set audio volume expression. <code>outpu: Set audio volume expression. output_volume = volume * input_volume
Set frame rate (Hz value, fraction or ab: Set frame rate (Hz value, fraction or abbreviation).
Set logging level and flags used by the: Set logging level and flags used by the library.
Set maximum output value for rematrixing: Set maximum output value for rematrixing. This can be used to prevent clipping vs. preventing volume reduction. A value of 1.0 prevents clipping.
Set optional x264 parameters to the enco: Set optional x264 parameters to the encoder.
Set optional x265 parameters to the enco: Set optional x265 parameters to the encoder.
Set pixel format. Use -pix_fmts to show: Set pixel format. Use -pix_fmts to show all the supported pixel formats.
Set the audio sampling frequency. For ou: Set the audio sampling frequency. For output streams it is set by default to the frequency of the corresponding input stream. For input streams this option only makes sense for audio grabbing devices and raw demuxers and is mapped to the corresponding demuxer options.
Set the number of audio channels. For ou: Set the number of audio channels. For output streams it is set by default to the number of input audio channels. For input streams this option only makes sense for audio grabbing devices and raw demuxers and is mapped to the corresponding demuxer options.
Set the video display aspect ratio speci: Set the video display aspect ratio specified by aspect.
Sets the display aspect ratio stored in: Sets the display aspect ratio stored in the file. It does not resize the pixels; players stretch the picture to this shape when showing it.
Shifts the audio later to fix sync.
Simple audio dynamic range compression/e: Simple audio dynamic range compression/expansion filter.
Skip the decoding and encoding step for: Skip the decoding and encoding step for the specified stream, so it does only demuxing and muxing.
Smooths out banding, the visible stripes: Smooths out banding, the visible stripes in gradients such as skies. Useful on heavily compressed sources.
Specifies a maximum tolerance. This is o: Specifies a maximum tolerance. This is only used in conjuction with -bufsize.
Specifies a minimum tollerance to be use: Specifies a minimum tollerance to be used.
Specifies the GOP (Group of Pictures) si: Specifies the GOP (Group of Pictures) size. This option is currently only supported by the x264 encoder.
Specifies the decoder buffer size, which: Specifies the decoder buffer size, which determines the variability of the output bitrate.
Specifies the target (average) bit rate: Specifies the target (average) bit rate for the encoder to use.

Target average bit rate. Add a unit: 300: Target average bit rate. Add a unit: 3000k is 3 Mbit/s. A bare number means bits per second, so 2000 is only 2 kbit/s. Required for two-pass.
The -profile:v option limits the output: The -profile:v option limits the output to a specific H.264 profile. Some devices (mostly very old or obsolete) only support the more limited Constrained Baseline or Main profiles. You can set these profiles with -profile:v baseline or -profile:v main.
The audio encoder. Pick one that the con: The audio encoder. Pick one that the container supports and your players can decode.
The file format that holds the video and: The file format that holds the video and audio streams. It decides which codecs you can use and where the file will play.
The file or stream to read. Use the prot: The file or stream to read. Use the protocol picker to fill in a URL template for FTP, HTTP, RTMP, SRT and so on.
The file to write, always the last argum: The file to write, always the last argument. Its extension follows the container chosen on the Format tab.
The removegrain filter is a spatial deno: The removegrain filter is a spatial denoiser for progressive video.
The resampling algorithm used when resiz: The resampling algorithm used when resizing. It only applies when a size is set.
The video encoder. It decides compatibil: The video encoder. It decides compatibility, file size for a given quality, and how long encoding takes.
Trades encoding speed for compression. S: Trades encoding speed for compression. Slower presets make a smaller file at the same quality; faster ones finish sooner with a bigger file. Pick the slowest you have patience for.
Updates are checked against the project: Updates are checked against the project GitHub releases. No media is uploaded.
Use -tune to change settings based upon: Use -tune to change settings based upon the specifics of your input.
Use hardware acceleration to decode the: Use hardware acceleration to decode the matching stream(s).
What to do when the custom size has a di: What to do when the custom size has a different shape from the source.
Where the clip begins, as HH:MM:SS (frac: Where the clip begins, as HH:MM:SS (fractions like 00:01:30.5 work) or plain seconds. Placed after -i, so ffmpeg seeks accurately but reads from the start of the file to get there.
Where the clip ends, measured from the s: Where the clip ends, measured from the start of the input, not the length of the clip. Same format as the start time.
Where the ffmpegd daemon is listening. F: Where the ffmpegd daemon is listening. From an https page, a daemon on another machine must be served over https.
Which side the Size preset applies to. W: Which side the Size preset applies to. Widescreen sets the width; Full Screen sets the height. The other side follows the source aspect ratio.
Windows x64 builds from Gyan. Downloads: Windows x64 builds from Gyan. Downloads are verified with SHA-256 and stored separately for each version.
Your encoding progress and logs will app: Your encoding progress and logs will appear here.
